solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Composer's wife getting grip of exercises with piano? Rubbish

indicators.note: to get a grip of something is to hold it inside one's grasp, so the wife's name wraps round the exercises

blocks.note: Clara Schumann, pianist wife of the composer Robert Schumann
PT is physical training
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A composer's wife, practising her keyboard exercises at the piano, dismisses the whole thing as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Clara Schumann was a celebrated pianist, so the piano in the surface fits her, but here it is just its musical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense, empty talk designed to win applause, so it is a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Lady's skin condition: one after opening has look inside

indicators.note: having something inside means holding it within, so the opening encloses the next piece

blocks.note: a chasm is a deep opening in the ground
lo! is an old exclamation meaning look
a means one

explanation.surface: A woman's skin complaint: after a first glance, the doctor looks closer inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One after opening' means the one comes after the opening, at the end of the answer, once look is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloasma is a patchy brown discoloration of the face, common in pregnancy, so it is chiefly a woman's skin complaint.

clue.text: Scrubber prince put up pocketing cash

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means it reads from bottom to top
pocketing means tucking something away inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Prince Hal, Shakespeare's young Henry V
oof is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A grubby prince is put up somewhere and slips the cash into his pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal reversed is LAH, which then holds OOF: L(OOF)AH.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is the dried fibrous pod of a gourd, used as a bath sponge for scrubbing the skin.

clue.text: Knavery in Shakespeare, irregular when the monarch's involved

indicators.note: involved here means wrapped up within, so the monarch sits inside the other word

blocks.note: patchy means uneven or irregular
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's knavery seems irregular whenever the king gets involved in it.
explanation.walkthrough: PATCH(ER)Y. Shakespeare uses the word once, in Timon of Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchery is Shakespeare's word for botched work or roguery, hence knavery.

clue.text: Article that's painful for old slave

blocks.note: the is the definite article
ow is what you say when something hurts

explanation.surface: A newspaper article on the hardships suffered by slaves of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A theow was a slave or thrall in Anglo-Saxon England, so it is a historical term for a slave.

clue.text: Neckline feature, dandy buttonhole?

blocks.note: a dandy roll is the roller that marks watermarks in papermaking, so dandy suggests roll
to buttonhole someone is to collar them, stop them to talk

explanation.surface: A dandy's neckline, featuring a flower in the buttonhole.
explanation.walkthrough: The dandy and buttonhole suggest a fop's lapel flower; instead they are the papermaker's dandy roll and the verb meaning to accost.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll collar is one that turns over and folds back around the neck, a common neckline design.

clue.text: 'Dutiful', suggesting French ranker?

blocks.note: first meaning: devout, showing duty to God or parents
second reading: the word looks like a plural of piou, from piou-piou, slang for a French infantry private

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: the word reads as though it were several pious, from piou-piou, the nickname for a French foot soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Pious describes religious devotion and dutiful respect, as in Virgil's pious Aeneas.

clue.text: Camel hair coating successful group

blocks.note: first meaning: a coarse fabric woven from camel or goat hair, used for coats (also spelt aba)
second meaning: the hugely successful Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: A pop group's camel-hair coats make them look successful.
explanation.definitionFit: Abba is both a Chambers word for a camel-hair cloth used for coats and the name of the chart-topping Swedish band.

clue.text: Almost stranded, on being kept in – arthritic condition?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
something kept in is held inside, so this small word goes within the other

blocks.note: a stranded whale is beached
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone almost stranded, kept indoors, suffers what may be arthritis.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: arthritis is one cause of aching bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone-ache is pain in the bones, which arthritis or rheumatism can cause, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A ——, Asian, modifies appearance of Indian sahiba

definitions.text: A ——, Asian, modifies appearance of Indian sahiba

indicators.note: to modify is to alter, and the clue says these letters alter into another phrase

blocks.note: taken as written: the letters the composite matches
taken as written: removed from the composite
taken as written: removed from the composite

explanation.surface: An Asian forehead dot alters how an Indian lady looks.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus A and ASIAN rearranges into INDIAN SAHIBA, so take A and ASIAN from those letters and the rest is the answer. The whole clue is also its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bindhi, or bindi, is the decorative dot worn on the forehead by Hindu women, changing a woman's appearance.

clue.text: A dimwit accounting for cow, old

blocks.note: taken as written
a daw, the jackdaw, is an old word for a simpleton

explanation.surface: A dimwit is held responsible for an old cow.
explanation.walkthrough: Cow is the verb, to intimidate, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adaw is a Spenserian verb meaning to subdue or daunt, as to cow someone does.

clue.text: Dominant Malagasies hard on drifters denied grants

indicators.note: being denied something means having it taken away, so the following word is removed from the drifters

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
o' is a clipped form of on, as in 'o' nights'
vagrants are people who drift from place to place
taken as written: these are the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A ruling people treat the island's drifters harshly, refusing them any handouts.
explanation.walkthrough: VAGRANTS with GRANTS taken away leaves VA; O' for on is an old poetic contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hova were the dominant people of Madagascar, the Merina, so the name stands for those leading Malagasies.

clue.text: Ape concealed in old raincoat? The opposite

indicators.note: in says one thing is placed inside another, here read with the coat and the concealment
the opposite flips which part holds which, so the coat goes inside rather than outside

blocks.note: hid means concealed
O is the abbreviation for old
a mino is a Japanese straw raincoat

explanation.surface: A man in an old raincoat hides an ape under it, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the ape would hide in the coat; 'The opposite' swaps the roles, so old raincoat goes inside concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hominoid is any member of the superfamily of great apes and humans, so an ape is one.

clue.text: Poet's confused in fancy hotels, one of the taps having come off

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine or invent, so the word that follows is to be rearranged
something that has come off is no longer attached, so that letter is dropped from the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written: the anagram fodder
a basin's taps are marked H and C, hot and cold

explanation.surface: A poet is bewildered in posh hotels where a tap has fallen off the basin.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the H from HOTELS and rearrange OTELS. 'Poet's' marks a Spenserian form.
explanation.definitionFit: Loste is Spenser's spelling of lost, and lost means bewildered or confused.

clue.text: Lizard from Indian territory, North America

blocks.note: Goan means from Goa, a former Portuguese territory, now a state, on India's west coast
NA is the abbreviation for North America

explanation.surface: A lizard is reported as originating from India or North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' belongs to the wordplay, not a link: from Goa is the adjective Goan.
explanation.definitionFit: A goanna is a large Australian monitor lizard, the name a corruption of iguana.

clue.text: Watching too much TV, maybe, turn oddly edgy, filled with joy

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so this word's letters are arranged strangely
filled with means holding something inside, so the joy goes within

blocks.note: a go is a turn
taken as written: the fodder
glee is joy

explanation.surface: A TV addict turns strangely jittery, then fills with joy.
explanation.walkthrough: The goggle-box is British slang for the television, which makes the definition apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Goggle-eyed means staring with wide eyes, as viewers glued to the screen are.

clue.text: Food for clue as an anagram, unsatisfactory to jewellers

indicators.note: the clue openly says these words are to be taken as an anagram, a cheeky self-referential signal

blocks.note: taken as written: all eleven letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A setter muses that some words are good food for an anagram clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Jewellers call a gem off-coloured when its tint is not the pure or desired shade, which lowers its value.

clue.text: More than one sauce vessel, vulgarly flashy? Tart obscured

indicators.note: something obscured is hidden from view, so those letters vanish from the word

blocks.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
an upstart is a vulgarly pushy person who has risen too fast
taken as written: the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A sauce boat looks vulgarly flashy, and the tart vanishes behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove TART from UPSTART to leave UPS, and add it to KETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ketchups is the plural of ketchup, a tomato sauce, so more than one sauce.

clue.text: Dyestuff, rich, stirred in jar

indicators.note: stirred means mixed about, so these letters are mixed into a new order
in places the mixed letters inside the jar

blocks.note: an olla is an earthenware jar
taken as written: the fodder

explanation.surface: A rich dye is being stirred in a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: The stirred letters go after the jar's first letter, not at its middle as one might expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchilla is a variant of orchil, a violet dye made from certain lichens.

clue.text: Line that's jagged, irregular etc penned by poet

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so these letters are shuffled
penned means shut in a pen, so the shuffled letters sit within the poet

blocks.note: Dante Alighieri, Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
taken as written: the fodder

explanation.surface: A poet pens an irregular, jagged line and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: Dancette is a heraldic term, so the poet's 'line' is a border on a coat of arms, not a line of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancette describes a line or border with large zigzag indentations, so a jagged line.

clue.text: NZ farm hand who may be ordered to hose pen endlessly

indicators.note: ordered here means put into order, so the letters are rearranged
without an end means the final letter of the last word is cut

blocks.note: taken as written
pen with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: A New Zealand farm worker gets told to hose down the sheep pen without end.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's farm chores fit the answer, who would indeed hose down pens.
explanation.definitionFit: In New Zealand a sheepo is a shed hand who brings sheep in from the pens for the shearers.

clue.text: I peak, coming from behind, ahead of a top golfer

indicators.note: coming from behind means read from the back, so the words are taken right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
a crag is a rocky peak
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer comes from behind to peak, finishing ahead of the top player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming from behind' sounds like a golfer's late charge; it reverses I CRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergio Garcia is a Spanish golfer who won the Masters and was a Ryder Cup stalwart, a leading player.

clue.text: Some popular timps backing, high-hat-like?

indicators.note: some of means only part of the words is used, a run of letters across them
backing means moving backwards, so the run of letters is read right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of popular and the start of timps

explanation.surface: Popular kettledrums back up the hi-hat cymbal in a drum kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The high hat here is a bishop's tall hat, the mitre, not the hi-hat cymbal the drums suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mitral means shaped like a bishop's mitre, a tall headdress, as with the heart's mitral valve.

clue.text: Box as a precaution

blocks.note: first meaning: to enclose in a case, a verb
second meaning: read as two words, just to be safe

explanation.walkthrough: Box looks like a noun but is the verb, to encase.
explanation.definitionFit: Incase is a variant of encase, to enclose in a box, while the split phrase means in the event of need.

clue.text: Eruption, hot, in Iceland and going of explosively – little new

indicators.note: going off means departing, so the conjunction leaves the country's name
something blown apart explosively lands in a jumbled new order
in places one letter inside the rearranged country

blocks.note: H for hot, as on a tap
taken as written
taken as written: the letters to remove
a little of new is its abbreviation N

explanation.surface: A hot volcano in Iceland goes off explosively with something small and new.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a volcanic eruption, but this eruption is on the skin. 'Going of' is a misprint for going off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lichen is also a skin disease marked by eruptions of small papules, so it is a kind of eruption.

clue.text: Surface gloss, well-known in a wing

indicators.note: in here means placed inside, so one word lies within the other

blocks.note: an el is an extension or wing of a building, in American usage
a name, as in a big name, is someone well-known

explanation.surface: A well-known figure in one wing of a building gives it a glossy finish.
explanation.walkthrough: E(NAME)L.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a hard glossy coating or paint applied to a surface.

clue.text: Accommodation going up in smoke (in Edinburgh?)

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: rooms are accommodation

explanation.surface: Lodgings are going up in smoke in Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up in smoke' reads as a fire, but 'going up' is the reversal and 'smoke' the definition, a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoor is Scots for to smother, and also to smoulder or smoke, so suitable for Edinburgh.

clue.text: River entering lake mistaken for a famous bay

indicators.note: something mistaken is wrongly put, so these letters are put in a different order
entering means going inside, so the river abbreviation goes into the other word

blocks.note: taken as written: the fodder
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A river flowing into a lake is mistaken for a famous bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Bay is not water but a horse's colour: the famous bay is the racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkle was the bay steeplechaser who won three Cheltenham Gold Cups in the 1960s, a celebrated horse.

clue.text: There's nothing fine, alas, in this offensive label

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
ay, as in 'ay me', is an exclamation of woe

explanation.surface: Sadly, there is nothing fine about this offensive slur.
explanation.definitionFit: Ofay is a derogatory US slang term used by Black Americans for a white person, so an insulting label.

clue.text: Family of fishes from America hide with camouflage

indicators.note: camouflage disguises a thing's appearance, so the letters are disguised by rearrangement

blocks.note: taken as written: all eleven letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A family of American fish hides itself using camouflage.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimaeridae is the zoological family name of the chimaeras or ratfish, cartilaginous fishes related to sharks.

clue.text: Car protected by French patron

indicators.note: something protected is surrounded and shielded, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for French
an auto is a car

explanation.surface: A car is safeguarded by a French benefactor.
explanation.walkthrough: The car goes inside the French: F(AUTO)R.
explanation.definitionFit: A fautor is an old word for a patron or supporter who favours someone's cause.

clue.text: Artist recalled exploit with centre of picture

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards
the centre of a word is its middle letter, taken alone

blocks.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: An artist remembered for exploiting the focal point of a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Klimt was the Austrian Secession painter famous for The Kiss.

clue.text: Flowering plant acquired from shop, deal negotiated

indicators.note: a negotiated deal has been worked over and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written: the fodder

explanation.surface: A flowering plant was bought from a shop at a negotiated price.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family plant with spikes of white or yellow flowers, the flower of Elysium in myth.

clue.text: Unconventional writing system fast losing following

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so a letter disappears from the word

blocks.note: fleet means fast
f is the abbreviation for following, as in pp. 6f

explanation.surface: A quick, unusual shorthand falls behind and loses its followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Leet, or leetspeak, is an internet alphabet that swaps letters for numerals and symbols, an unconventional way of writing.

clue.text: Barmy stuff formerly essential for dyesters

indicators.note: the essential part of something is its core, so the letters lie within the word

blocks.note: the four letters after the opening d

explanation.surface: Some crazy substance was once indispensable to people who dye cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Barmy is not 'mad' here: barm is the froth on fermenting malt liquor, so barmy stuff is yeast.
explanation.definitionFit: Yest is an obsolete spelling of yeast, and barm is the yeasty froth on brewing beer.

clue.text: Get cross about a bed, collapsed, that's 'ready to mount'?

indicators.note: a collapsed bed has fallen into a disordered heap, so its letters are rearranged
about means around, so the word for get cross wraps the rest

blocks.note: rile means to anger, making someone cross
taken as written: the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone gets annoyed when a bed collapses just as it was 'ready to mount'.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks flag a playful definition: something you can ride is ready to be mounted.
explanation.definitionFit: Rideable describes a horse or a track fit to be ridden, so it is ready to mount.
